title: Fletcher Henderson's mistakes, and the band leaving Chick Webb on the road
summary: Fletcher could not play after Benny Goodman performed his arrangements first, and the band once left an unpaid Chick Webb by the roadside.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: I don't think anybody that you know now, but I did some of the arranging for the band in those days, too, as well as the Apollo Theater. That's about as much as I can elaborate on Snowden. I think it's worth mentioning about another one of our great leaders. I mentioned his name before. I've been connected with Fletcher from his time -- first arrival in New York up to the time he passed. But I remember -- Fletcher made a lot of mistakes as we all have, and they always say Fletcher died of frustration, and a lot of those things were of his own doing -- I know that. For example, you know, he was the chief arranger for Benny Goodman, and we were both scheduled to play at Savoy the same night, and every arrangement he made for Goodman he made a copy for himself for his band. But Goodman went on ahead of us -- we couldn't go on, because every number that we were going to play, Goodman had played ahead of us. And we couldn't go on. The people yelled, so they said, "Well, he's chicken. He's afraid to complete against Benny Goodman." And that hurt him worse than anything else. And there were more of his mistakes. Now, Chick Webb, before the advent of Ella Fitzgerald, the band wasn't in demand like it became later on. He owed us for so many gigs we'd done and he didn't pay, so finally out on Long Island one night we finished playing the dance -- there was no money, so we were passing a wooded area of Long Island and we just opened the car and put Chick and his drums and books right out on the

road. It's 4:00 o'clock in the morning. He said, "I don't care, I don't care." Put him out on the road with his drums, his books and everything, and ran off and left him. So, it was blowing up a storm, so the driver said, "I better go back and get him." You know, when we went back to get that rascal, he's sitting there in the pitch dark in the woods, he said, "I don't care, you didn't have to come." And he wasn't as big as a --
Sitting right there. "You didn't have to come back and get me."
The band put him out. I was one of them that helped push him out. Oh, he was a great little guy, though.
